target_customer: School districts, foodservice operators and later retail buyers of plant-based chicken products
problem: Plant-based meat cost far more than animal meat, which kept it out of schools and cafeterias. The company set out to reach price parity through automated, high-throughput manufacturing equipment.
business_model: B2B plant-based chicken sold to foodservice and schools, plus proprietary manufacturing equipment and process know-how
product_category: Plant-based meat manufacturing technology and foodservice products

founders.name: Christie Lagally
founders.background_notes: YC page and Food Dive (April 2020) describe her as a former Boeing engineer; YC page cites nearly 20 years of engineering experience and 5 manufacturing technology patents. Education not found in an opened source.

technical_complexity.rationale: The pitch required inventing and building continuous, automated food manufacturing equipment to hit cost parity, which is capital intensive and slow for a small team. The YC page cites 5 manufacturing technology patents held by the founder.

defensibility.rationale: Patented equipment and process know-how are hard to copy quickly, but plant-protein recipes and product formats are easy for large food companies to replicate once the cost curve is proven.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A June 2019 Spoon article expected competition to grow, especially once Tyson launched a plant-based line, and said few plant-based chicken firms targeted B2B foodservice at the time. No source found shows an incumbent acquiring or copying the equipment approach.

market_need_then: In June 2019 The Spoon reported that few plant-based chicken companies targeted foodservice. The company's own pitch is that plant-based meat was too expensive for mass adoption, and school districts later signed on (108 districts by February 2023 per Green Queen headline).

branding.name_origin: The company launched as Seattle Food Tech and rebranded to Rebellyous in June 2019. The Spoon says the name was meant to express lighthearted but determined efforts to make plant-based meat accessible to everyone; no literal etymology is given.
branding.domain_note: Company site is rebellyous.com. Earlier domain not found.

identity.logo: Not described in any opened source
identity.voice_and_tone: Punny and lighthearted, for example the tagline No Harm. No Fowl. and the site line made with love, care, and no birds

branding.brand_signature: No Harm. No Fowl. (trademark applications filed by Seattle Food Tech in 2020)

rebrands.why: The Spoon says the old name did not resonate with customers the way Beyond Meat or Impossible did and partners wanted a name that described the brand

brand_strength.rationale: A deliberate rebrand to a playful, memorable name and a trademarked tagline, but no evidence of mascot, community or merch pull. Sold mainly B2B, so consumer awareness was limited.

outcome_analysis: Rebellyous is still operating and has raised a Series A in 2020 and a further $9.5M equity round in 2023 backed by the same lead investors, which suggests steady but modest progress in a plant-based meat sector that hit a demand slump after 2021. The founder's aerospace manufacturing background fits the equipment thesis. Whether price parity at scale was reached is not shown by public sources, and no shutdown or acquisition was found in an outcome search.
notes: Competitors left empty: searches found only 2019 sources (The Spoon June 2019, Nosh 2019 on Gardein and Tyson), which are about a year after the S18 batch, so none were listed. Unverified funding: a roughly $250K seed dated 2019-10 (StartupIntros only), a $5.35M 2021 raise attributed to PitchBook, and a $2.47M Series B-III in 2025-01 (CB Insights and VCBacked). The Spoon says just over $2M had been raised by June 2019, a pre-Series A amount that I could not itemize. Totals conflict: CB Insights says $20.44M, Green Queen says over $30M. The GeekWire 2019 profile returned HTTP 403 and was not read. The 2023 round is labeled Series B by StartupIntros but the cited article gives no label, so stage is other.
